accuracy.evidence: Checked against AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462 sections 4.2.1.2 (ionic bonding: electron transfer from metal to non-metal giving noble-gas structures), 4.2.1.3 (giant structure held by strong electrostatic forces acting in all directions) and 4.2.2.3 (high melting points; conduct when melted or dissolved because ions are free to move). Values: Na 2,8,1 to Na+ 2,8; Cl 2,8,7 to Cl- 2,8,8; NaCl coordination number 6 (rock-salt structure), 4 in a flat slice; NaCl melts at 801 °C, MgO at about 2852 °C; formulas NaCl, MgCl2, MgO, CaCl2, AlCl3 balanced by charge.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented GCSE bonding misconceptions (Taber's molecular framework): NaCl as discrete molecules or ion pairs (tag pair, step 2 prediction 'only its own Cl- partner'), electron sharing in ionic bonds (tag share), metal ion given a negative charge (tag sign), unbalanced formulas such as MgCl (tag ratio), ionic bonds being weak (tag weak), solid ionic compounds conducting because they contain ions (tag solid) and free electrons carrying current in a melt (tag elec).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagionlat is about the lattice itself: a tappable 5x5 lattice that draws every attraction on one ion, a 3x3 build grid that refuses like charges side by side, a 1:2 Mg/Cl lattice counted to a formula, a temperature slider where vibration grows until the lattice breaks at 801 °C, and a conduction cell with solid, molten and dissolved states. flagion forms single ions, flagcov shares electrons and flagsimol covers simple molecules. Lab gate overlap under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Students see that the dragged electron completes both outer shells and makes opposite charges, discover four pulls on an inner ion (no partner), get 'two Cl- side by side repel' when they misplace an ion, count 6 Mg2+ to 12 Cl- before choosing MgCl2, watch the ions jiggle harder until the lattice collapses at 801 °C, and find the bulb lights only when ions can move. Step text confirms each finding afterwards.

predictions.evidence: Six predictions with tempting wrong options that the lab disproves: 'Na-, it changed' for the sodium ion, 'only its own Cl- partner', 'like charges in rows', 'MgCl', '100 °C' for the melting point and 'Yes, ions are charged' for solid salt conducting.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight challenge questions with shuffled answers; every distractor carries a tag (pair, share, sign, ratio, weak, solid, elec) whose feedback names that slip, e.g. 'Ionic compounds have no free electrons. The current is carried by moving ions.'

readability.evidence: Learner text reads at FK about 4.7 and adult text about 6.3, both inside the validate_lessons targets (6.5 and 9.5) while keeping the GCSE terms students are examined on: electron transfer, electrostatic attraction, giant ionic lattice, oppositely charged ions, molten, dissolved.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate is clean. Each learner paragraph adds one idea (electron transfer, lattice not molecules, formula from charge balance, properties from structure), and each lab step demonstrates exactly one of them; the adult text names spec points, data and seven mistakes.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the 1.15 tall canvas shows the 5x5 lattice with Cl- discs about 52 px and labels at 13 px, the build grid squares are about 70 px, formula chips are about 95 x 55 px, the temperature thumb is 26 px with +/-100 °C buttons as twins, and no caption is clipped at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (Move the electron to Cl, Tap the middle/corner ion, Add Na+ / Add Cl-, Count the ions, formula buttons, -100/+100 °C, Test solid/molten/dissolved); the canvas aria-label is updated with each spoken result; continuous jiggle animation stops under reduced motion; walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone.

sources: AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) specification, 4.2.1.2 Ionic bonding, 4.2.1.3 Ionic compounds, 4.2.2.3 Properties of ionic compounds
CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics: melting points of sodium chloride (801 °C) and magnesium oxide (2852 °C); rock-salt structure with coordination number 6
Taber, K. S. (1998) 'An alternative conceptual framework from chemistry education', International Journal of Science Education 20(5): the molecular framework misconception about ionic lattices
